proposal: The Mandate says the next Administration should adopt a posture calling for a fully sovereign Mexico, meaning one not controlled by criminal cartels, and take available steps to support that outcome quickly. It says the same Administration should use that posture and work with other Western Hemisphere partners to halt the flow of fentanyl, including precursors from Chinese manufacturers. The text is general and names no specific instruments.

status_summary: Executive Order 14157 (signed 2025-01-20) directed steps to designate cartels as foreign terrorist organizations, and State's designation of eight groups took effect on 2025-02-20 (90 FR 10030), six of them Mexican cartels including the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG; two more Mexican groups, the Juarez Cartel and Los Viagras, were designated effective 2026-07-16 (91 FR 43721). Mexico transferred 29 alleged cartel figures to the US in February 2025 and 26 more on 2025-08-12, and CRS reports a total of 92 by January 2026. A joint statement of 2025-09-03 created a US-Mexico security implementation group, whose fourth meeting on 2026-06-12 reaffirmed cooperation with full respect for each country's sovereignty, and in March 2026 the US launched an Americas Counter Cartel Coalition with other regional governments, which Mexico has not joined. 25 percent IEEPA tariffs on Mexican imports from March 2025 were withdrawn after the Supreme Court's 2026-02-20 ruling, per CRS; the President has also repeatedly threatened unilateral military action in Mexico, which the Mexican government opposes.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14157 directed designation of cartels and other organizations as foreign terrorist organizations and specially designated global terrorists.

State's notice designating eight organizations as foreign terrorist organizations, including six Mexican cartels (Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, Carteles Unidos, Cartel del Noreste, Cartel del Golfo and La Nueva Familia Michoacana), takes effect on publication (90 FR 10030, Public Notice 12672, signed 2025-02-06).
Mexico expelled 26 alleged cartel members to the US, the second such transfer after 29 in February 2025.
A US-Mexico joint statement during the Secretary of State's visit to Mexico announced a security implementation group, per CRS.
The Supreme Court held IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; CRS reports the 25 percent IEEPA tariffs on Mexican imports, in place from March 2025, were withdrawn.

The Americas Counter Cartel Coalition was launched in March 2026 with the US and 16 Latin American and Caribbean countries, later 19 members; Mexico is not a member, per CRS (the day is not given; the first of the month is used as a placeholder).
At the fourth meeting of the security implementation group, officials reaffirmed cooperation with full respect for each country's sovereignty.
State's notice designating the Juarez Cartel and Los Viagras as foreign terrorist organizations takes effect on publication (91 FR 43721, Public Notice 13065, signed 2026-07-02).

title: Adopt a 'sovereign Mexico' posture against cartels and work to halt fentanyl trafficking
uncertainties: The coalition's launch day in March 2026 is not given by CRS, so the timeline uses the first of the month as a placeholder. The tariff and coalition details rely on the CRS report rather than the underlying orders and announcements, which were not read. The 2025-02-20 and 2026-07-16 designation notices were read in full on federalregister.gov in this review (90 FR 10030, signed 2025-02-06; 91 FR 43721, signed 2026-07-02); the State fact sheet was read only as republished by GlobalSecurity. The Mandate's fentanyl reference includes Chinese precursor makers; China-directed duties and fentanyl measures were not examined here (see c02-19). Reports of a covert lethal operation in March 2026 were denied by both governments, per CRS, and are not relied on. Inference: the match is parallel because the text sets a general posture without instruments; in_progress reflects several operative steps without a defined end point.
